On the same days, Russia attacked another foreign commercial vessel sailing under the flag of Antigua and Barbuda near Odessa, killing one crew member and injuring three others. Another civilian vessel under the flag of Republic of Marshall Islands was struck in the port of Odessa, leaving four crew members injured. Within less than 48 hours, Russia attacked three separate foreign merchant vessels operating near Ukrainian ports. Ukraine expresses its deepest condolences to the families and all seafarers and port personnel killed in these attacks. Russian attacks caused injuries among civilian seafarers from Ukraine, Egypt, Syrian Arab Republic and India. Thus, such attacks have an impact on interests of many members of this organization. These facts are difficult to explain as coincidence or accident. These are deliberate actions. Since 22nd July 2026, maritime exports through Ukraine sports have been suspended as a result of Russian attacks on civilian commercial vessels. The implications of the fact are obvious, and the timing of these attacks is particularly revealing. They are taking place at the height of harvest season when millions of tons of Ukrainian agricultural products are expected to reach global markets. According to Ukrainian authorities, since the beginning of July alone, 31 merchant vessels have come under attack. Russia understands perfectly well what the consequences for such actions may have. More than 90% of Ukraine agriculture exports pass through Black Sea ports. Such attacks put the pressure on global food markets and increase uncertainty for countries that depend on Ukrainian agricultural export. And the consequences are felt far beyond Ukraine and Europe. Millions of families in Africa, Asia, Latin America, and Middle East ultimately pay the price when the grain shipments are disrupted, transport costs increase, and commercial shipping becomes more dangerous. Mr. President, in 2022, with the help of the Secretary General Antonio Guterres and our Turkish partners, we established the Black Sea Grain Initiative. It made an important contribution to global food security. Russia later withdrew from the initiative unilaterally. Having taken that decision, it subsequently attempted to place responsibility on the United Nations and the Secretary-General. We have categorically rejected such allegations. It's Russia who withdrew from the initiative by its own choice, disrupted a mechanism that benefited countries across multiple continents, and now questions the role of the institutions that helped make that mechanism possible. Delegations can assess these facts for themselves. Ukraine, in part, expresses its full support for the Secretary-General and his consistent position in defense of the Charter of the United Nations, international peace, and international security. We have launched the maritime corridor in the Black Sea in order to support these efforts. while Russia continues to target them with missiles and drones. One important fact should not be overlooked. Nobody is attacking Russian grain routes, striking Russian merchant vessels, or destroying its grain terminals. Ukraine implements its right to self-defense guaranteed by the UN Charter with the caution and respect for international law. Our forces attack only Russia's military potential and facilities which support Russia's war machine. We never wanted this war. When Ukraine strikes military airfields, military bases, ammunition and fuel facilities that support Russian war effort, the war simply returns to where it originated. On the contrary, Russia attacks Ukrainian ports, grain terminals and commercial vessels, and expects the international community to accept such terror. Russian terror against civilians and the threats to global food security must end. The United Nations must make full use of all appropriate tools at its disposal, including those provided by international law, to put an end to attacks against civilians, restore freedom of navigation in the Black Sea, and ensure the safety and security of seafarers who continue to suffer from these attacks. Defending freedom of navigation has long been a priority for the Security Council, and we take note of its recent initiatives and resolutions addressing these actions of destructive actors threatening maritime security on important international routes. The deteriorating situation in the Black Sea also requires the urgent attention and action without further delay. And we also would welcome those good offices that would help ensure Russia's full compliance with its obligations under international law, including the law of the sea. Mr. President, yet Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine extends far beyond the missile strikes, attacks against ports, or attempts to disrupt global food supplies. While the world sees burning ships in the Black Sea and destroyed apartment buildings in Ukrainian cities, Tens of thousands of Ukrainians remain trapped behind prison walls in the temporarily occupied territories and inside Russian Federation itself. Their only crime was defending their country, refusing occupation, speaking Ukrainian or remaining loyal to their homeland. 96% of released Ukrainian prisoners of war interviewed by the OHCHR reported torture or other forms of ill treatment, Nearly 90% reported conflict-related sexual violence. At least 109 Ukrainian prisoners of war have been executed after capture, while dozens more have died in custody. Civilian detainees have been subjected to the same machinery of abuse. Torture remains widespread and systematic. At least 182 civilians have been executed in areas under Russian control, including in places of detention, Many others never returned alive from captivity. The return of all our citizens is of paramount importance for us and the United Nations and the international community, and we should play an active role in this process. Every day spent in Russian captivity is another day of suffering that international law was created to prevent. The return of every prisoner of war and every legally detained civilian as well as unlawfully deported Ukrainian children, must remain an international priority until the last Ukrainian comes home. Mr. President, the picture that emerges from everything we have discussed today is remarkably consistent. Whether we speak about missile strikes against residential neighborhoods, attacks against grain terminals and merchant vessels, or torture chambers hidden behind the prison walls, we are dealing with different manifestations of the same policy. As Voltaire once famously said, those who can make people believe absurdities can make people commit atrocities. This is what Russian society is going through. And those responsible bear full responsibility for these war crimes. Moscow does not cherish the lives of its own citizens. Its imperial ambitions remain at the top of its agenda. All efforts by Ukraine and our allies to restore peace have been met with escalation by Russia. Everything indicates today that Russia is preparing for a new wave of mobilization, destruction, and deaths. And as President Zelensky recently indicated, Russia wants 30,000 more troops from the DPRK to support the operation. Yet another demonstration of the Kremlin's regime malicious intentions was drenched by the history lesson delivered by the Russia's ruler yesterday evening. His distorted understanding of history and the world, coupled with yet another attempt to shift blame for the regime's own crimes onto others, is far more than effort to justify Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine. It is a diagnosis of an entire system that can survive only by feeding on bloodshed, suffering, and fear. Such rhetoric once again exposes the true nature of the Kremlin regime, one built on lies, violence, and imperial ambition. Thus, we call on our partners to put all efforts into real steps which will restore comprehensive, just, and lasting peace. This requires increasing support for Ukraine, strengthening pressure on Russia, and further weakening its war capabilities. And we also echo the same request that was announced today by our partners. It's time for action, not deliberations. Thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the representative of Ukraine for that statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Estonia.

Thank you, President. I have the honour to speak on behalf of the Baltic States. We align ourselves with the statement of the European Union. Now in the fifth year of its full-scale aggression against Ukraine, Russia shows no signs of abandoning its imperialistic objectives in subjugating Ukraine. Recent weeks have seen some of the most intensive aerial attacks since the full-scale invasion began. Combined missile and drone strikes hit cities across Ukraine, killing and injuring civilians and destroying homes, hospitals, schools, and other essential infrastructure. A Russian strike on a UNICEF warehouse in Bilohorodka destroyed humanitarian supplies worth nearly $4 million. On the 24th of July, a Russian strike destroyed the premises of Latvia's honorary consulate in Sloviansk, in clear violation of international diplomatic norms. We condemn these unlawful and deplorable attacks in the strongest possible terms. Unable to break Ukraine's resistance, Russia seeks to terrorize the population through intensified so-called human safari drone attacks near the front lines. Attacks against civilians and civilian objects, as well as indiscriminate attacks, are prohibited under international humanitarian law. Destroying essential infrastructure on which millions depend serves no legitimate military purpose. The same pattern is evident in the Black Sea. With the harvest season underway, Russia is attacking grain-carrying civilian cargo ships. leaving dozens of international crew members from Egypt, Syria, India killed and injured. Deliberately disrupting Ukraine's maritime export corridor, Russia is targeting global food markets, raising risk of hunger on millions in Africa, Asia, and the Middle East. We call on this council and the wider international community to condemn these attacks and demand that Russia cease them immediately. We also express our solidarity with Romania for the repeated drone incursions into their airspace. Russia's reckless behavior needs to stop. Mr. President, Russia's armed and security forces have been repeatedly listed in annexes to the Secretary-General's reports for grave violation against children and are now also listed for conflict-related sexual violence. following the verification of 310 cases of such violence against Ukrainians. Security Council Resolution 2242 welcomed the Secretary-General's decision that all countries repeatedly listed in the annexes to his reports are prohibited from participating in UN peacekeeping operations. Forces repeatedly implicated in these abuses cannot credibly protect vulnerable populations under the UN flag. We urge the Secretary General to apply this decision consistently and the Council to uphold and implement its unanimously adopted resolution. We urge Russia to immediately end the indoctrination and militarization of Ukrainian children. and ensure the return of all those unlawfully deported and forcibly transferred. We also urge Russia to release all Ukrainian prisoners of war and unlawfully detained civilians and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need, including in Ukraine's temporarily occupied territories. Every victim deserves justice and Russia's actions must be met with accountability. We support the International Criminal Court and the swift establishment and operationalization of the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine. We call on all member states to support and assist the ICC and the Special Tribunal in their mission to fight impunity, bring justice to victims, and prevent future international crimes. The Baltic States reiterate their call for an immediate, full and unconditional ceasefire as the first step towards a just and lasting peace in Ukraine, grounded in the UN Charter and international law. Such peace cannot be imposed upon Ukraine or reward aggression. We will continue to stand with Ukraine and reaffirm our unwavering support for its independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. I thank you.

I.

Thank the representative of Estonia for that statement. I now give the floor to Mr. Quentin Weyler from the delegation of the European Union to the United Nations.

Thank you, Mr. President. I have the honor of delivering this statement on behalf of the European Union and its member states. The candidate countries, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Albania, Ukraine, the Republic of Moldova, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Georgia, as well as Andorra, align themselves with this statement. I thank the DRC presidency for convening this meeting, and I thank the briefers for the factual updates. The death and destruction caused by Russia's unprovoked aggression against Ukraine continues unabated. The UN has verified over 2,000 civilian casualties in June alone, the highest in four years. Almost all occurred in Ukraine's urban centers as a result of Russian aerial bombardments. While the world demands a ceasefire and negotiations, Russia responds with brutal attacks against Ukraine cities and their population. Last week, it destroyed Latvia's honorary consulate in Sloviansk, and as others in this room, I express full solidarity with Latvia. We are now also seeing a trend of attacks against humanitarian workers bringing relief to people living close to the front lines. By every standard set for itself, Russia is not achieving its objectives. It spends 40% of its budget on its military and security. It has suffered over a million casualties for minimal territorial gains. It stands isolated internationally and its economy is under heavy strain. The fact that this cynical brutality against civilians is now fueled by Russia's desperation with its failure on the battlefield excuses neither its inhumanity nor its blatant violations under international law. In fact, it compounds them both. The EU continues to stand firmly in defense of international law as enshrined in the UN Charter. We will continue to support Ukraine in exercising its inherent right to self-defense under Article 51 of the Charter. We have mobilized over 200 billion euros this year, all in response to an illegal invasion by a permanent member of this Council. We continue to call for a full, unconditional and immediate ceasefire, as well as a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in Ukraine based on international law, including the UN Charter. We call on Russia and its ally Belarus to immediately ensure the safe and unconditional return of all unlawfully deported and transferred Ukrainian children. We urge all countries, including the members of this Council, to cease any assistance or diplomatic cover to Russia, whether direct or indirect. Colleagues, Russia cannot succeed in changing borders by force or in escaping accountability for its actions. The sooner Russia realises this and the sooner it ends its aggression and comes to the negotiating table, the sooner this senseless cycle of death and destruction has a chance to end. We urge all members of this Council to work with us in pressuring Russia to do so and to ensure full accountability for war crimes and the other most serious crimes committed in this war of aggression. The time for a ceasefire is now. I thank you, Mr. President.
I thank Mr. Weiler for his statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Poland.

Mr. President, I thank the Democratic Republic of the Congo for convening this meeting. I would also thank the briefers. for the informative presentations. Despite heavy losses on the battlefield and mounting economic problems, Russia remains unwilling to end its war of aggression against Ukraine. On the contrary, it systematically targets Ukrainian civilian infrastructure, causing civilian casualties and depriving thousands of people of access to essential services. Last week, Russia added the honorary consulate of Latvia in Slovyansk to the list of targets of its strikes. Poland condemns these actions in the strongest possible terms and calls yet again on Russia to stop the war. The recent escalation of Russian attacks against Ukraine's Black Sea ports and commercial vessels is already disrupting maritime traffic and poses a serious threat to Ukraine's export capacity, particularly with regard to agricultural products. These deliberate attacks undermine not only Ukraine's economy, but also global food security and the fundamental principle of freedom of navigation. Poland strongly condemns the recent drone incursions into Romanian airspace. Russia's provocations, especially across the eastern flank of NATO, from Estonia through Poland to Romania and other allies, are clear violations of international law. Mr. President, this Council has repeatedly heard Moscow's narrative about the alleged root causes of the war and its so-called legitimate security concerns. These are propaganda slogans that bear no resemblance to reality. It is time to stop repeating these narratives and instead focus on the facts. Ukraine was not a NATO member in February 2022, nor was its accession imminent. Claims that Ukraine or NATO posed a threat to Russia's sovereignty were never supported by the strategic realities preceding this invasion. Indeed, one listens to Russia's bizarre justification for this war. it becomes increasingly difficult to understand what really objectives Moscow claims to be pursuing. Its explanations are detached from reality. We therefore call on all members of this council to reject these false narratives and remain guided by the facts. And the fact is that Russia's revisionist neo-colonial policy long predates 2022. For years, Moscow has sought to preserve a sphere of influence over its neighbors through military aggression, coercive diplomacy, economic pressure, cyber operations and disinformation. This is not the behavior of a state acting in self-defense. This is the behavior of a state pursuing domination and imperialism. Russia's rhetoric about the legitimate security concerns reflects its outdated imperial mindset rather than the genuine response to an immediate threat. It is Russia that has become the principal source of insecurity in Europe. The only way to address the so-called root causes of this war is for Russia to change its own policy. In the meantime, Ukraine has an inherent right to defend itself against Russia, as enshrined in Article 51 of the UN Charter. Mr. President, the path to peace is clear. It requires pressure on Russia by the international community, including the members of this Council, so that Russia finally engages in meaningful negotiations. We call on all the United Nations Member States committed to peace, international law and the Charter to strengthen these efforts. And I thank you.
I thank the representative of Poland for the statement. There are no more names inscribed on the list of speakers. The meeting is adjourned.
